title: Chemsha Bongo Reflection and Mental Check-In Questions
description: 160 reflection prompts organized by topic, including the original 100 questions and 60 additional original prompts for mental check-ins, gentle distraction, open-ended discussion, perspective, support, and next steps.

questions.question: Are you uncomfortable discussing anything from past events?
What would you say about your early years?
What are a few of your favorite childhood memories?
What characteristics and beliefs have been influenced by your past?
Is there a particular moment in your life you would like to share about how your values or viewpoint changed significantly?
Do you still feel the effects of any major past events on you now?
Would you like to go back and revisit any past experiences?
Do you have a special family ritual or tradition from your early years that you cherish?
Do you see any recurring themes or patterns in your earlier experiences? If so, how do you deal with them in your present life?
How does nostalgia affect your current feelings and what part does it play in your thoughts about the past?
Do you feel that unresolved problems from previous experiences are impeding your happiness or personal development?
What aspects of your past decisions—both successful and unsuccessful—still affect the way you make decisions now?
What effects did the good and bad relationships you had in the past have on your capacity to trust people?
In three words, how would you sum up your emotional condition right now?
Which certain situations or incidents make you feel happy?
How do you manage intense feelings on a daily basis?
Is there a particular memory from your early years that still affects your feelings now?
How do your fundamental concepts influence the way you feel and behave?
Is there a good way for you to let out your anger? How do you do that?
Do you have any feelings that you usually repress? If yes, why?
What effects do your feelings have on the people you interact with?
Which forms of self-care do you use to keep your emotional health in check?
Can you identify any stress or anxiety-related emotional triggers in your life?
How do you tell the difference between real feelings and ones that are influenced by other forces?
Do you have any particular objectives in mind to strengthen your emotional resilience?
Regarding the emotional development, how at ease are you with vulnerability?
How can self-reflection help you recognize and control your emotions?
What would you say best describes the primary thoughts that cross your head every day?
Would you like to look into any negative thought patterns that seem to come back?
What is your approach to dealing with self-critical thoughts, and how do they affect your sense of worth as an individual?
Is there anything that you can see that might be causing you to perceive reality differently?
How much do your current cognitive processes originate from your previous experiences?
Are you prone to having intrusive or nervous thoughts in certain situations?
What is your procedure for making decisions, and are there any particular ideas that get in the way?
Do you have any instinctive beliefs that exacerbate stress or feelings of being overwhelmed?
What effects do your thoughts have on your capacity to establish and accomplish goals?
In what ways do you strike a balance in your everyday thinking between acceptable and inappropriate ideas?
Do you see any patterns of thinking that might be causing problems in your relationships?
What effects does your self-talk have on your determination and ability to persevere in the face of difficulty?
Are you always thinking about any unsolved problems or unanswered questions?
How do you deal with overthinking, and does it make it harder for you to unwind?
Which techniques do you regularly use to encourage constructive and optimistic thinking?
What benefits do your present healthful activities provide for your general well-being?
Do you have any particular daily practices that promote your mental and physical well-being?
How well do your food choices support your overall wellness and health objectives?
Do you have any bad habits that you think might be affecting your general health?
As sleep is essential to living a healthy lifestyle, how do you prioritize getting enough of it?
How do you stay motivated to be active? What part does regular exercise represent in your daily routine?
What particular methods or strategies do you employ to handle stress in every aspect of your life?
How do you keep a balanced fluid intake throughout the day and make sure you’re properly hydrated?
To enhance your mental well-being, do you engage in mindfulness or meditation practices? If so, how has it changed your day-to-day activities?
What actions do you take to keep a good work-life balance, and how has it affected your general well-being?
In everyday routine, how do you maintain a healthy relationship with technology and regulate screen time?
How do you respond to obstacles or failures in upholding your healthful patterns?
Do you adhere to any particular dietary guidelines or nutritional targets in order to maintain a healthy lifestyle?
How can your general health and well-being benefit from your relationships and social connections?
What effects do your underlying beliefs have on how you see the world and yourself?
Is there any belief that you can think of that limits your growth or well-being?
How have your relationships beliefs changed over time, and how do they affect how you connect with other people?
What fundamental beliefs do you have about success and failure, and how do they influence the way you tackle obstacles?
What aspects of your identity and decision-making are influenced by your cultural or religious beliefs?
Did you ever doubt or reevaluate some of your long-held beliefs? If so, why did you think that way?
To what extent does your mental and emotional health depend on what you believe about your own value and affection?
Which belief systems in your life can be a cause behind your tension or anxiety?
How can you better handle life transitions if your beliefs about change and adaptability are different?
Do any messages or beliefs from your early years still affect the way you think and act now?
How does your sense of purpose and involvement in the community stem from your political or social beliefs?
Which decisions and priorities in life are influenced by your beliefs about happiness and fulfillment?
Have you seen any changes in your beliefs as a result of remarkable experiences or personal development?
What are your methods for finding balance and how do you resolve contradictory beliefs inside yourself?
Could you describe a situation in which refuting or altering a certain belief resulted in a beneficial change in yourself?
In what ways does your present approach to building connections with others draw from your past relationships, both good and bad?
In your relationships, what are the most important values you look for, and how do they make you feel satisfied overall?
Do you see any trends in your previous relationships that you would like to alter or enhance?
What techniques do you employ to protect healthy communication in your relationships, and how do you handle conflict in them?
How do you handle disagreements in a relationship and what aspects of your expectations match those of your partner?
How do you strike a good balance and set priorities for your friendships, family ties, and romantic relationships?
How do you establish and maintain trust with others, and what part does trust play in your relationships?
What are some changes you would like to make to the way you give and receive love in your relationships?
Do you have any concerns or insecurities that might be getting in the way of your capacity to build and sustain meaningful relationships?
In order to build mutual respect and understanding, how do you establish and convey limits in your relationships?
Can you spot any trends in the way you decide on a career, and if so, how have they affected your route in the workplace?
What coping strategies do you employ to deal with the pressure and stress you face at work?
How does the career you’re pursuing now help you feel fulfilled and purposeful?
Is there anything that you are afraid of or insecure about that could be impeding your career growth? If so, how do you intend to overcome it?
In making job decisions, how do you strike a balance between following your passion and being realistic?
How important is work-life balance to your sense of overall job satisfaction?
How can you make sure your health and well-being are top priorities at work?
How do your professional decisions fit into your long-term financial objectives?
What is your definition of success in your career, and has it changed over time?
How does your perfect future appear to you?
Do you have any concerns regarding your future?
How well do your present objectives fit with your long-term plan?
Which goals are more important to you, long-term or short-term?
What impact do your core values have on your future plans?
How do you respond to unanticipated modifications to your long-term plans?
How do you strike a balance between your career and personal goals?
Do any self-limiting thoughts prevent you from pursuing your goals?
How do you handle uncertainty regarding the future in your life?
How do you make sure your plans for the future help you feel fulfilled?
What has taken up the most space in your mind today?
If your mood had a weather forecast, what would it be and why?
What feeling has been easiest to notice today, and what feeling has been harder to name?
What has felt manageable today, and what has felt heavier than expected?
What do you need more of right now: rest, connection, movement, clarity, or something else?
What is one thing that has helped you get through today?
What has surprised you about your mood or energy recently?
What would make the next hour feel a little easier?
What have you been carrying quietly that you might want to acknowledge?
If you could check in with yourself without judging the answer, what would you ask?
What are five things you can see around you that you have not paid much attention to?
Which sounds can you hear right now, from the nearest to the farthest away?
What is one object nearby, and how would you describe its shape, texture, color, and purpose?
What small detail in your surroundings feels interesting or comforting?
If you had to describe the room you are in to someone who has never seen it, what would you mention first?
What song, sound, or kind of music helps you feel more present, and what do you notice as you listen?
What is a simple activity that can occupy your attention for five minutes without adding pressure?
If you could take a peaceful walk anywhere familiar, what would you notice along the way?
What are three ordinary things around you that are useful, beautiful, or well made?
What small, harmless curiosity could you explore for a few minutes just for fun?
What topic have you wanted to talk about but have not found the right moment for?
What feels complicated in your life at the moment, and which part would you like to untangle first?
What do you wish people understood about your experience without you having to explain it repeatedly?
What question about yourself are you currently trying to understand?
What would you say if you knew you could be honest without needing to make your thoughts sound perfect?
Which part of your life feels most in need of attention, and why?
What is something you have changed your mind about recently?
What would a useful conversation about your current worries look like?
When you talk through a problem, what kind of response helps you most: listening, questions, practical ideas, or a different perspective?
What would you like to understand better about the way you react to difficult situations?
What story are you telling yourself about a situation, and what other explanations might also fit the facts?
Which parts of a current worry are known facts, and which parts are predictions or assumptions?
If a friend had the same thought you are having, how might you respond to them?
What evidence supports your current interpretation, and what evidence might you be overlooking?
Is there an all-or-nothing conclusion you are drawing, and what might a more balanced version sound like?
What thought keeps returning, and what might it be asking you to pay attention to?
How does your mood affect the way you interpret other people's words or actions?
What is within your influence in this situation, and what is outside your control?
What would you think about this problem after a good night's sleep or a little distance from it?
What is a kinder but still realistic way to describe what happened?
When stress builds up, what early signs do you notice in your body, thoughts, or behavior?
What has helped you cope with a difficult day before, even if it only helped a little?
What usually makes a hard moment more difficult, and what tends to make it more manageable?
Who could you contact if you wanted company, practical help, or someone to listen?
How could you ask for support in a way that makes clear what you need from the other person?
What boundary might protect your time, energy, or peace of mind this week?
What can you postpone, simplify, or ask for help with instead of carrying it all at once?
What does taking care of yourself look like when you have very little energy?
What would help you feel safer or more settled in your current environment?
If your usual coping strategy is not helping, what is one different, low-pressure option you could try?
What has mattered to you lately, even if it has not received much of your time?
Which personal value would you like your next decision to reflect?
What is one small action you could take today that would support the person you want to become?
What would progress look like if it did not have to be perfect or dramatic?
What can you give yourself permission not to solve today?
What is one thing you would like to make room for in your week?
What recent moment reminded you of something you care about?
What would you like to thank your past self for handling or learning?
What is one realistic thing you can look forward to, however small?
What would help you finish this reflection feeling a little clearer or more supported?

source_notes.title: WHO — Doing What Matters in Times of Stress
source_notes.use: General inspiration for grounding, noticing thoughts and feelings, values-based action, and self-kindness. The new questions are original wording, not copied exercises.

source_notes.title: NHS — Thought record
source_notes.use: General inspiration for separating situations, feelings, interpretations, evidence, and alternative perspectives. The new questions are original wording.

source_notes.title: NHS — How to talk about your mental health
source_notes.use: General inspiration for identifying trusted support and communicating what kind of help would be useful.

source_notes.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Grounding and the senses
source_notes.use: General inspiration for present-moment sensory attention and gentle grounding prompts.

usage_note: These prompts support personal reflection and are not a diagnostic tool or substitute for professional mental-health care. Let users skip questions or stop whenever they wish.
